clue.text: Perfidious crime, as air conditioning is for Jacob?

parts.words: as air conditioning is for Jacob
parts.note: the name JACOB pictures the letters AC, short for air conditioning, sitting in the middle of the name JOB

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about some treacherous crime and how a man named Jacob relates to his cooling system.
explanation.walkthrough: Look at how Jacob is spelt: AC sits in the middle of JOB, so AC's relation to Jacob is the answer. The question mark flags this backwards way of working.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime committed by someone within the organisation robbed, so a betrayal of trust from within.

clue.text: Intestinal problem purging insides of Estonian dramatist

parts.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome

indicators.note: clearing out the middle letters of the word Estonian leaves just its two ends

explanation.surface: A medical note about a gut complaint that has cleared out a playwright from Estonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purging insides of' removes everything but the first and last letters of Estonian, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Crazy Gang led by small US comedian

indicators.note: the crew comes after, following behind the letter for small, which goes in front

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a crew is a gang of people
Lucille Ball was the American comedian of I Love Lucy

explanation.surface: Evokes the Crazy Gang, a British comedy troupe, oddly headed by a small American comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crazy Gang was a famous British comedy troupe of the mid twentieth century, which makes 'Crazy Gang' read as one name.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwball is an eccentric, zany person, and the word also works as an adjective meaning wildly eccentric.

clue.text: Hide problem under mat — it isn't entertaining

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of holding or harbouring, so the words under mat it isn't contain the letters

explanation.surface: A grumble that something under the doormat is no fun at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' means hosting: the answer is held within 'under mat — it isn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide means skin, and this inflammation of the skin is a skin problem.

clue.text: Shaking milk container, seized by extremes of jollity

indicators.note: the milk container is grabbed and held between two outer letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here from jollity

parts.note: an udder is the bag on a cow that holds milk

explanation.surface: A wobbling milk jug gripped by someone in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of jollity' gives J and Y, which go around UDDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Juddery describes a vibrating, jerking motion, so it is a synonym for trembling or quivering.

clue.text: Rabid dog bite requiring treatment

indicators.note: the letters are treated or processed, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A bite from a dog with rabies needs medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabid' looks medical beside 'dog bite', but here it means fanatical, and 'requiring treatment' rearranges 'dog bite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid can mean extreme or fanatical in opinion, which is the sense of an intolerant, prejudiced person.

clue.text: Issue covered by arms programme

indicators.note: the letters are concealed under, so contained within, the words arms programme

explanation.surface: A political matter hidden inside a weapons programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a political matter, but it means offspring; SPROG is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring or children, and a sprog is a British slang word for a child.

clue.text: Talks endlessly about doctor

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for talking endlessly is read backwards

parts.note: yaps means chatters on and on without stopping

explanation.surface: Someone goes on and on about a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' looks like a signal to cut a letter, but it belongs with 'Talks' to give YAPS; 'doctor' is a verb, meaning to neuter an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor a pet is a euphemism for neutering it, and to spay is to sterilise a female animal.

clue.text: Retrospective acknowledgement: argon is noble gas

indicators.note: looking backwards, so the word for an acknowledgement and the symbol for argon are read in reverse

parts.note: a nod is a small gesture acknowledging someone
Ar is the chemical symbol for argon

explanation.surface: A belated admission that argon belongs among the inert gases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' looks like a description of the acknowledgement, but it signals reading backwards; Ar is the chemistry symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: This radioactive element sits in group 18 of the periodic table, the inert or noble gases.

clue.text: Stars on the radio are irritating breed

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: things that grate are irritating
to bear young is to breed

explanation.surface: Celebrities heard on air are an annoying type of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' seems to mean celebrities, but it is the constellation. 'on the radio' signals GRATE heard as GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a northern constellation, a group of stars containing the Plough.

clue.text: Noisy sleeper leaving Pole more vexed

indicators.note: a pole departs, so its letter is removed from the noisy sleeper

parts.note: a snorer sleeps noisily
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A loud sleeper's Polish partner walks out, making them even crosser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the north pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore can mean annoyed or aggrieved, so sorer is the comparative: angrier, more irritated.

clue.text: Stroke head of grumpy old man during picnic

indicators.note: during means within, so these letters go inside the word for a picnic

parts.note: a picnic is something easy, as is a doddle

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Hitting the head of a bad-tempered elderly man at an outdoor meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' and 'picnic' both read literally; a stroke is a swimming style and a picnic means something easy, as in 'no picnic'. DODDLE is British for an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: The doggy paddle is a simple swimming style, a basic stroke where the swimmer paddles like a dog.

clue.text: Modern masters keeping books for folk in rag trade?

parts.note: modern means new

indicators.note: the masters hold the books within themselves

parts.note: sages are wise masters
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Up-to-date master tailors holding on to books, as people in the clothing business might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag trade' usually means the clothes business; here a rag is a newspaper, so the people are those who sell papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a slang term for a newspaper, and these shopkeepers sell newspapers and magazines.

clue.text: One can initially use boomerang

indicators.note: a boomerang comes back, so the letters return the other way

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of use

explanation.surface: An Australian suggesting that a single person may throw a boomerang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boomerang' is a verb here, turning TIN + U back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing or the number one, a quantity regarded as a whole.

clue.text: Rider somehow ran amok

indicators.note: running amok is wild and disorderly, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider who somehow went wild and ran out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amok' rearranges the letters of 'somehow ran'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female equestrian is a rider of horses.

clue.text: Giving tea and sympathy after penny dropped

parts.note: char is a British slang word for tea

indicators.note: the penny is dropped, so its letter is taken away from sympathy

parts.note: pity is sympathy
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: Offering tea and sympathy once someone finally understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penny dropped' is the idiom for understanding at last, but here it removes P from PITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity is generous giving to people in need, so the noun matches the act of donating.

clue.text: Kid rings sister with unusual problem

indicators.note: the word for kid encircles the sister

parts.note: to cod is a dated British word meaning to kid or hoax
a nun is a religious sister
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A child phoning a sibling about an odd difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is a verb meaning tease, giving COD.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question or a difficult riddle.

clue.text: Desperate entrance and exit

parts.note: a door is an entrance
to exit life is to die

explanation.surface: A frantic way in and way out, as if fleeing a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exit' is used in its theatrical and euphemistic sense of departing life.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-or-die effort is a desperate one where everything depends on success.

clue.text: Road rage in part of African colony

parts.note: a drive is a road, as in street names
to rant is to rage loudly

explanation.surface: Aggressive driving in part of a former African territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African colony' suggests empire; it is an ant colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Driver ants are African army ants that live in vast colonies, so one is a member of such a colony.

clue.text: Silly people regularly unveil inventions

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word unveil

parts.note: lies are invented stories

explanation.surface: Foolish people routinely reveal new gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'unveil', N E L.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelly is a British informal word for a foolish or weak person, as in 'big nelly'.

clue.text: Extremely talented mate with new business

parts.note: a star performer is extremely talented
to tup is for a ram to mate with a ewe

explanation.surface: A gifted friend has a fresh company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' looks like a friend, but it is the verb, as a ram mates.
explanation.definitionFit: A start-up is a newly established company, usually a small young firm.

clue.text: British-American bank having bigger assets

parts.note: a tier is a bank, as in a row of seats or levels

explanation.surface: A transatlantic bank with larger assets on its balance sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assets' looks financial; here it hints at a fuller figure. 'bank' is a row or level, a TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Busty means having a large bosom, and the comparative describes someone more well endowed.

clue.text: Bony half-cut artist in wine shops

indicators.note: only the first half of the word bony is kept, the rest is cut

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French painter

explanation.surface: A thin, tipsy painter sits in wine shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British for drunk, apt in wine shops, but it keeps half of 'Bony'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar, and in the US a small grocery.

clue.text: Ham producer, articulate woman of wisdom

indicators.note: articulate means spoken aloud, so the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a wise woman is one who knows things, a knower

explanation.surface: A meat producer who is also a well-spoken wise woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' suggests meat, but Ham was one of the patriarch's three sons in Genesis. In a non-rhotic British accent KNOWER sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch of the ark fathered Ham, Shem and Japheth, so he produced Ham.

clue.text: American saying proper farewell

indicators.note: saying something says it out loud, so it is the pronunciation that counts

parts.note: due means proper or fitting

explanation.surface: An American expression for a correct goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saying' sounds DUE as the French DIEU, as English speakers often say it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French word for goodbye, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Scottish families ignoring fences — dismal experiences for lairds?

indicators.note: the fences are the outer letters, which are left out

parts.note: clans are Scottish families
downers are depressing experiences

explanation.surface: Clans ignoring boundaries make for gloomy times for the Scottish gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring fences' drops the first and last letters of CLANS, leaving LAN. A laird is a Scottish owner of a landed estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish estate owner, so lairds are examples of property holders, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Runner runs over line, wailing

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so first

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An athlete runs past the line, crying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete but is a ski, which runs on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirl is the shrill, piercing sound of bagpipes, a wailing noise.

clue.text: Ultimately, eating rubbish made me fat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A rueful admission that eating junk food put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: the clarified butter used in Indian cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is clarified butter used in South Asian cooking, a cooking fat.

clue.text: Berlin building site founders touring Switzerland in torment

indicators.note: the rest goes inside the word for torment

parts.note: to rag is to tease or torment

indicators.note: touring means going around, so these letters surround the code for Switzerland
founders means collapses, so the letters of site fall apart and re-form

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A building site in Berlin collapses while touring Switzerland in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'founders' rearranges site as EIST; 'touring' wraps that around the Swiss code; 'in' puts the lot inside the word for torment. 'Berlin building site' wants to be one phrase but splits after building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag is the historic parliament building in Berlin, home of the Bundestag.

clue.text: Recollection of lame setter in US resort

indicators.note: re-collection, gathering back, signals reading the word backwards

parts.note: to lame is to maim, as a verb
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: A memory of a limping crossword setter at a Florida holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lame' is a verb here, MAIM, which 'Recollection of' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a beach resort city in Florida, United States.

clue.text: Think about old piece of computer equipment

indicators.note: the thinking word goes about, around, the letter for old

parts.note: to muse is to think deeply

explanation.surface: Pondering an antique computer component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places MUSE around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is the hand-held pointing device used with a computer.

clue.text: A tot plans to play after end of term

indicators.note: the letters are free to play around and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A toddler makes plans to play once the school term is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like a school term but is the end of pregnancy, the full term.
explanation.definitionFit: Postnatal means following childbirth, which comes at the end of a pregnancy's term.
